name: sh2-test-grammar
description: The machine-readable grammar of the `test("...")` string — the frontends' condition channel (py-sh-go `test("$x -gt 1")`, c-sh-go `test("$a -eq $b -a ...")`, every frontend lowers its languages' conditions into it). Frontends must DERIVE their condition lowering from this spec instead of rediscovering the grammar by trial. The authoritative implementation is `parseTest`/`evalTest` in harness/sh2-namespace.mjs; this file is the contract documentation (core request frontends-test-grammar-20260806).
input: A single string; the runner tokenizes it by splitting on whitespace (the shell's word-splitting already happened on the frontend side — each operand is one token, expansions pre-evaluated).

argument_count_semantics.1 token: true iff the token is non-empty — even when it LOOKS like an operator (`[ -gt ]` is a string test); a lone `!` is false (the empty string)
argument_count_semantics.2+ tokens: parsed with the precedence grammar below

precedence.name: primary
precedence.note: parenthesized group `( expr )`, unary flag, binary comparison, or a bare string (truthy iff non-empty)

unary_flags.note: a dangling flag with no operand (`[[ -n $x ]]` with x empty) evaluates against the empty string (`-n ""` is false)

string.==: equal (glob pattern when the rhs contains glob chars)
string.=~: rhs is an ERE regex matched against lhs (documented guarantee — the runner implements it)

integer.note: non-integer operands make the WHOLE test false (bash: integer expression expected, exit 2)

expansion_rules.$var: the variable's value at test time — the frontend emits `$name` text; the runtime expands it (or the emitter inlines lifted bindings)
expansion_rules.quoting: the test string is ONE string — the frontend is responsible for embedding its operands (quote-joined) so whitespace inside an operand survives
expansion_rules.split: the runtime does NOT field-split inside the test string (word-splitting happened at tokenization on the frontend side)

tags.double_bracket: the A1 test call may carry a trailing `[[` tag arg (extglob-nocasematch-20260806): double-bracket style = no word splitting, extglob patterns, =~ regex, no empty-arg ambiguity

semantics.exit_status: the test evaluates to true/false; the runner records it as lastExit (0/1) for `&&`/`||`/if/while contexts
semantics.native_lowering: the ESTree emitter may lower tests to NATIVE JS comparisons when the operand values are statically safe (numeric ops on lifted numerics, string equality on store-free values); the native forms must agree with this grammar
